lead: the friend you have had longest is the one you never took anywhere. nothing was ever wrong with her life, no route was needed, and thirty years in you could not say what the two of you actually do.
sun: every other friendship you have began the same way: somebody in a bad year, a way through it that only you could see, four months of walking it with them, and then the edge of the country they were trying to reach. The Guide hands you a complete form of friendship with the ending already in it. you can date the end of all of them, and none of those endings was a quarrel.
moon: what puts you on the road is The Blaze: a nose for the part of a person's situation they have not worked out yet. point it at somebody with nothing wrong and it comes back empty. the friendship with no road in it gives your curiosity nothing to work on either, which leaves the longest attachment of your life as the one you cannot describe.
pull: every friendship you can describe had a route in it. the one that has outlasted all of them is the one neither of your talents has ever found a use in.
tension: twice she has asked what is wrong, in the tone of somebody braced for the answer, and nothing is wrong. an afternoon with her puts you on the same footing as a border with the walking finished, and what comes over you there has never had anything to do with her. saying that would land as an insult, so she keeps the version in which you went off her by degrees, for no reason she can name.
cost: four months, no debt afterwards — that is what it takes you to get somebody out of the worst year of their life, and the record is long. what the same instinct cannot do is an ordinary wednesday. thirty years of the one friendship that never needed you has been kept going by her, and she has never mentioned that.

lead: you got him the whole way there, over two years, and what that room has of it is the ninety seconds at the end of the party, with a glass in your hand.
sun: the two years left no record. the appointments, the money, the drive to his brother's — he came through it and what he carries is that he got himself out, which is roughly correct, and is how a good crossing registers on the person taken. so your whole contribution to that man sits where nobody can point at it, and it ended, on purpose, at the edge of the life he has now.
moon: The Storm has one setting, and the place it found was the far edge, on the night the road ran out and no next thing existed. what went up in that room had two years of pressure in it and came out in one piece, at the size it had been inside you, in front of his family and yours. it landed entire, and outlasts the two years.
pull: two years of it had no witnesses and ninety seconds of it had forty. what the room kept is the ninety seconds, and they do not come off.
tension: the reading settled within a week: you could not let him have his day, and there is something possessive in it. none of it can be answered, because the only person who could describe the two years is the man whose evening you took, and asking him to do that is the same act again. he half-carries the room's version himself now. it comes up at every gathering, as a joke, and the joke is nine years old.
cost: nobody in that man's life had to be told they were being carried, which is the whole reason it worked, and it worked for eleven people before him. the road ends and the evening does not: you stop, nothing follows, and what is left standing is at full volume. the eleven each tell one story about you, and they tell the same one.

lead: nobody had closed anything. the list still had your name on it, the trade had changed in three ways you did not know about, and on the first evening back after eleven years your hands went ahead of you.
sun: a route does not go stale. the eleven years took nothing off it, because what you hold is the order of things and the places people give up, and neither of those has moved. what actually stopped, back then, was not the ability — the last one got across, you turned round at the edge, and nothing came after. you called it a change of direction at the time and everybody accepted it.
moon: nothing at your end was ever shut, so there was nothing to reopen — The Return files a leaving as an interval and you were simply on it again, and inside a month the eleven years had no size. what that covers is what the eleven years actually were: the longest stretch you have ever spent with nobody in front of you, and it never got named as one.
pull: you did not come back to it. nothing had ended, and eleven years is what an edge looks like when nobody hands you the next person to walk.
tension: two of the three you rang were delighted. the third asked you not to again, and she was right to. she had to finish the thing herself, alone, in the year after you went, and your name coming up eleven years later put her back at the start of that. from where you stand nothing had been ended, so nothing was being restarted, and that is the part she cannot use. the other two tell people you never left.
cost: eleven years cold, and you were useful inside a week — the route keeps without maintenance, which is why anybody who needs taking somewhere gets the full version of you now and got it at thirty. what has no sentence available is why you went back. the years off it had nobody to take anywhere, and this is the only thing you own that comes with a next step.

lead: he died on a tuesday afternoon with everything in order, nineteen months after you took it on, and by the friday there was nothing in front of you at all.
sun: the consultants, the sister who would not speak to him, the flat, the will, and the thing he was actually frightened of, which took until the spring to get out of him — nineteen months of route, and it worked. he got there the way he had wanted to. his own account, right to the end, was that he was managing, and that is what a delivery feels like from inside.
moon: what is standing where the route was has no edges on it, and from any distance it reads as grief, and gets treated as grief, because grief is a shape people know how to bring things to. up close there is nothing in it to mourn with. the road ended and no instruction came for the afternoon, and The Ghost puts no outline on that for anybody, yourself included.
pull: nineteen months had a next step in every hour of it. the friday had none, and the thing that stands in you where the road was is not made of missing him.
tension: his widow rings on sundays, two years on, and his sister rings when something needs deciding, and both of them describe it as keeping an eye on you. the traffic runs the other way and always has. correcting it would mean saying that the nineteen months ended cleanly and what came after them was not sorrow, and every version of that sentence sounds like somebody who did not love him.
cost: almost nobody will take on the last stretch of a person's life and stay to the end without needing to be thanked for it. that part you did faultlessly. what the walking does not come with is anything for the friday — an afternoon, a turned-round walk home, and a hundred earlier versions of that same edge have taught you nothing about this one.
